rules.title: Short vowel + ck: back, pick, luck
rules.short_explanation: At the end of a short word, write ck for the /k/ sound after a short vowel: back, pick, luck, clock, truck. After a long vowel, two vowels or a consonant, write just k: make, book, bank.
rules.tts_text: After a short vowel, the k sound is written ck.
rules.mnemonic: Short vowel, strong end: ck. Long vowel or consonant: just k.

examples.text: I need a quick answer today.
He packed the boxes into the truck.
Please look at the clock on the wall.
She picked a ripe apple from the tree.
examples.note: Pick has a short vowel: use ck.

examples.text: He has a sore neck after the flight.
Good luck with your exam!
The lock on the door is broken.
She wore black shoes to work.
Please make a list of the boxes.
examples.note: Long vowel a: use k, not ck.

examples.text: The bank opens at nine o'clock.
examples.note: After the consonant n: use k.

examples.note: Long vowel a: write just k.

examples.note: After a consonant: write just k.

examples.note: Two vowels oo: write just k.

rules.title: The f sound as ph or gh: phone, laugh
rules.short_explanation: The /f/ sound is not always written f. In many words from Greek it is ph: phone, photo, alphabet, physics, phrase. In a few common words it is gh: laugh, enough, tough, rough, cough.
rules.tts_text: The f sound can be written ph or gh.
rules.mnemonic: Phone and photo: ph. Laugh, enough, tough: gh.
